doc: Keynorm cross-language parity vectors (S4b-main T1). Script-generated pins: expected outputs of training/keynorm.py, mirrored byte-identically by src/inference/keynorm.{h,cpp} and pinned from BOTH sides (tests/test_keynorm.cpp + training/tests/test_keynorm.py). Corpus-derived provenance; corpus files themselves stay absolute (normalization is a load-time view).

enriched.note: ENRICHED chord (inversion/tension/name carried): only `root` may move, every other key of the input chord dict must survive the shift unchanged - the C++ shape is authoritative (phase-B B11, decision D-B11). The C++ reader is ints-only, so the per-chord tension list is flattened to one int per chord (-1 = no tension); the type/name names stay in-test spec constants on the C++ side.

known_divergence: NONE - healed in phase-B tranche E B11 (owner decision D-B11): the C++ shift_chords_to/from_canonical and the python shift_chords now agree on the chord SHAPE - only `root` moves (clamped 0..127) and every other key of the input chord dict (type/inversion/tension/name) is preserved as-is. Pinned from BOTH sides over the enriched vector in #chord_parity.enriched; the corpus-level parity on {root, type} chords is unchanged.
